title: OVRCR approved gallery palette transfer
scope: The 80 previewed gallery variants only. Excludes the three research-only families. This package contains palette research/mappings and no OVRCR code changes.
protected_existing_rules: Do not create duplicates for the eight existing themes.
Do not replace existing palette values, aliases, serialized identifiers, default selection, or persisted user settings with gallery approximations.
Resolve exact existing IDs in the current OVRCR source. Gallery IDs are stable transfer IDs, not assertions of current local IDs.
Preserve approved gallery names and IDs as metadata. New native IDs may follow repository conventions if the mapping is explicit and collision-free.
The six protected existing themes other than Mocha/Latte are upstream preview adaptations, not verified copies of current OVRCR token values.
Mocha/Latte were inspected at the listed commit; still preserve the current local definitions.
implementation_contract: All 80 should be represented in the Settings browser, with 72 additions plus the eight protected existing choices.

Settings must group by explicit appearance_group (Dark/Light). Do not infer appearance from RGB brightness. Keep family and high-contrast metadata within those groups; high-contrast labels are source variant names, not accessibility certification.
Preview temporary selection without clobbering the saved theme; explicit apply persists; cancel restores the prior selection. Align exact UX with existing Settings conventions.
Preserve the canonical source palette alongside mapped OVRCR roles. Do not blindly import editor activity-bar or selected-row colors with mismatched foregrounds.
Review all derived, reused, composited, or untraced roles and pair-level contrast flags before shipping.
Status meaning must not rely on hue alone, particularly Vesper, Oxocarbon, and low-contrast light variants.
Dashboard theming must not recolor independent agent PTY output.
Carry forward applicable upstream attribution and license notices. No proprietary theme packages or research-only palettes are included.
